page1.text:
The memory of the man who was set up as a hero.
The story of a knight whose end came to a place that I can't reach.

page2.text:
That hill is his world.
The desolate wasteland that the man obtained by fighting for others.
Apparently he died smiling in satisfaction, holding on to this view.

page3.text:
"...He's seriously stupid."
...Yes, that just makes me seriously mad.
He tried his best, worked hard even though he was an ordinary person, and finally obtained a miracle with his own blood.
Then it'll be a lie if he doesn't become happy.
If he made many people happy, then he had to become happier than all those people combined.

page4.text:
But, he did not receive such a reward.
The only thing he was given was the fate to be used as a Guardian after his death.

page5.text:
...
That's right. Why didn't I realize that?
Guardians are summoned into every age.
Doesn't that mean that they are summoned from every age?
In other words, from the present and the past.
And Heroic Spirits can even be summoned from the future we have not yet seen.

page6.text:
For Guardians who are pushed into a position off of the axis of time, the concept of time does not exist.
At the point that they became a Heroic Spirit, they sublimate into something other than what they used to be when they were human.
Then...
It is possible for a Guardian to be summoned into the place and age they lived in when they were alive.

page7.text:
...
It's vexing when I think about it.
It's because neither of them gets salvation.
The one that watches his past self...
or the one that watches his eventual self...
They will only hurt by how they changed.

page8.text:
I already know the end of this big idiot who tried to be of help to others.
He became a Guardian by choice.
He thought that it was more than he could ask for if he could save people even after he died.
He did not have the power to save people when he was alive, but he believed that he could break through any tragedy as a Heroic Spirit.

page9.text:
Thinking so, he made a contract with the world to give his body after death, and saved hundreds of lives.
He believed he would be able to save tens of thousands of people and more after that.

page10.text:
But, he was betrayed by such hope.
Places where Heroic Spirits and Guardians appear are only hell.
They only appear when the world is about to be destroyed by people.
Humans are beings that perish by their own doings.
That's why the process of destruction should always be the same.

page11.text:
He was only summoned to those "hells."
In the land where the ones he wanted to save were already dead, he killed even more people.
The boy who said he just didn't want to see anyone cry...
...Could only see humans crying forever.

page12.text:
There is only one thing I can say.
He has been betrayed by many things the whole time.
And in the very end, he was even betrayed by the only thing he believed in, his ideal.

page13.text:
I am the bone of my sword.
Steel is my body, and fire is my blood.
I have created over a thousand blades.
Unknown to Death,
nor known to Life.
Have withstood pain to create many weapons.
Yet, those hands will never hold anything.
So as I pray, UNLIMITED BLADE WORKS.

page14.text:
...That was the only spell he was given.
What is that?
It makes me so mad that I want to beat his chest and scold him.

page15.text:
...I, Rin Tohsaka, have never had any hardships in my life.
So I might not have the right to say it, but I believe in working hard and going through pain. It's wrong not to be rewarded for your battles.
That's why I'm angry at his unrewarded life, and most of all... I can't leave him, who ended up cursing his life, be.

page16.text:
"As long as you're my Servant, I won't do anything other than what I believe in.
I'm not as naïve as Shirou Emiya, but there are still things that I cannot give up.
No matter who it is, I don't have the intention of giving it up..."

page17.text:
...That's right.
That's why I swore that...
As long as I'm his Master, I will believe in my path like he used to do.

page18.text:
That's about all I can show to him.
That's about the only way I can repay him.
That might've been meaningless, but at least...
I do it so that Archer, who lost sight of his own past, could realize that his life was something he can be proud of...

page19.text:
"Ah... Mm..."
The first thing I notice when I wake up from my slumber are the sensations in my limbs.
They hurt, and I can't move them.
"...I'm tied up."
Plus, I'm sitting in a chair and seemed to be sleeping in an unnatural position.

page20.text:
...
...I don't want to admit it, but I'm in the worst possible situation.
To be honest, I can't do anything.
My hands are behind the chair and restrained by something like handcuffs.
My ankles are the same, and I can't stand from my chair.
On top of that, my handcuffs and shackles are magecraft-resistant, and my Magic Circuit is so messed up that I can't even create magical energy.

page21.text:
...
Now that I've confirmed my situation, I check my surroundings.
...It's cold.
The room made of stone has no heater, and it is an abandoned place that hasn't been used for a while.
It's dark outside the windows. From the looks of it, it's probably past 10 PM or so.

page22.text:
"So. What are you planning, Archer?"
I glare into the darkness.
...The shadow of the pillar.
The knight in red is sitting on a pile of rubble.

page23.text:
"Nothing. You are just bait to lure Shirou Emiya. You should know that."
"...Heh. Shirou would come even if I wasn't here. You should know that."

page24.text:
"...Yeah. But, it would be inconvenient if you were with him. I'll have you stay here quietly until things are settled."
Archer states without appearing in front of me.
There is no sign of previous intimacy.
He is really a calm assassin now.

page25.text:
"I see. So you will kill Shirou no matter what?"
"Yeah. A naïve man like that should be killed right now."
He replies, as if it's only natural.
The only thing I can see from here is his shadowed side profile.
His expression is cold, as if he's wearing a mask.
That...makes me seriously infuriated.

page26.text:
"...Heh. I don't even need to be told that Shirou is naïve."
I take a breath.
It'll end if I say this.
Archer will never come back to me if I say that.
I take a breath and stare at the man in the shadows.

page27.text:
"But still, I think that naïve part of him is lovable.
He needs to be like that. I'm saved by having a guy like him."

page28.text:
"But what about you?
You did this much, but you think it's wrong to preach a selfish ideal?
You fought for others again and again, got betrayed again and again, and you were forced to clean up after them again and again...!
Did you get fed up with humans from that, Archer...!?"
